summary.text: Direct preference optimization is used alongside safety alignment and instruction following to optimize model behaviors. Adversarial prompts trigger high-variance trajectories resulting from internal conflict between safety alignment and instruction-following objectives. This approach targets balancing safety alignment and instruction-following capabilities in language models.

target_user.text: No evidence in the bundle; hypothesis to test: AI engineers and developers who train and fine-tune large language models and require balanced safety and instruction-following performance.

jtbd.text: No evidence in the bundle; hypothesis to test: When deploying language models that handle sensitive queries, developers want to align models for safety without degrading general instruction-following capabilities so that applications remain robust and secure.

value_prop.text: No evidence in the bundle; hypothesis to test: Combining direct preference optimization with instruction following and safety alignment helps mitigate internal conflict and reduces vulnerability to jailbreaks.

riskiest_assumption.text: The riskiest assumption is designated on axis V (viability) due to missing evidence. It is assumed that paying customers are willing to adopt and pay for a specialized direct preference optimization and safety alignment toolkit.

mvp.text: Conduct customer interviews and a price acceptance test with AI engineering teams to validate willingness to pay for a tool that balances safety alignment and instruction following using direct preference optimization.
mvp.type: customer interviews and price acceptance test

success_metric.text: Proposed threshold: 40 percent of interviewed engineering leads express willingness to adopt and budget for the alignment solution.

kill_criteria.text: Proposed threshold: fewer than 10 percent of contacted engineering teams agree to a follow-up interview or price acceptance test.
